name: Abednego
summary: Abednego, first called Azariah, was one of Daniel's friends from Judah taken into the court of Babylon. With Shadrach and Meshach he would not worship the king's golden image, and God brought them out of the fiery furnace unharmed.

key_moments.title: Renamed Abednego in Babylon
key_moments.description: Azariah was among the young men of Judah chosen to serve in the king's court, and the prince of the eunuchs gave him the name Abednego. He and his friends ate vegetables and drank water instead of the king's food, and God gave them knowledge and wisdom.

key_moments.title: Set Over Babylon
key_moments.description: When the king's dream was a secret, Daniel asked Azariah and his friends to pray to the God of heaven for mercy. After Daniel told the dream, the king put Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in charge of Babylon's affairs.

key_moments.title: Refusing to Bow
key_moments.description: Abednego and his friends would not serve the king's gods or worship his golden image. They told Nebuchadnezzar their God was able to deliver them, but even if He did not, they would not bow.

key_moments.title: Saved from the Fiery Furnace
key_moments.description: The three were bound and thrown into a furnace heated seven times hotter. The king saw four men walking free in the fire, and when they came out not a hair was singed, so he blessed their God and promoted them.
